cues.en: System 5 IPC, it doesn't matter if, I mean, it doesn't matter if, first of all, it's, okay. It's System 5 IPC, so you are already, like, that's like Insta-rage. You don't even need to add anything. I mean, have you ever looked at the System 5 IPC? Like, what human hater wrote System 5 IPC? I mean, did Hitler write this interface? I'm serious. I mean, it's like, you have to hate people. I hate people, I hate programmers, and boy am I getting even with them.
cues.zh: System 5 IPC，不管是不是……我是说，不管怎样，首先它可是 System 5 IPC，光听到就让人秒炸毛。根本不需要别的借口。我是说，你们看过 System 5 IPC 吗？到底是什么仇恨人类的家伙写出 System 5 IPC 的？难道是希特勒写了这套接口？我是认真的。这得有多恨人类啊。“我讨厌人类，我讨厌程序员，看我怎么收拾他们。”

cues.en: These interfaces are terrible. But it's the kind of code that you touch at once, you should be able to get it working, it should be verifiable, and then people don't have to have like, oh, by the way, make FreeBSD unsecured so you can run Postgres without corrupting your data. It's like, whoa, what did you just say? So that's, I would say, a really important one. So I think the fact that those patches are there shows that a little bit of energy, I think, would get these things in. And then the really big one, to me anyway, is VImage or VNet.
cues.zh: 这些接口烂透了。但这种代码只要碰过一次，就应该能跑起来，应该能验证，大家就不用面对这种尴尬：“顺便说一句，把 FreeBSD 的安全防护关了，这样跑 Postgres 才不会搞坏数据。”听了直接让人愣住：等等，你刚才说什么？所以我觉得这真的很重要。既然补丁都在那儿了，只要花一点点精力，应该就能合进去。然后对我来说，真正的大头是 VImage 或者 VNet。

cues.en: which actually adds exclusive IP stacks to jails and actually is pretty exciting stuff. And this is one of these, and we'll get back to this in a little bit when we talk about zones, but this is an area where zones explicitly inspire jails. Where the folks that originally did this work were like, we want to make this more like zones by adding exclusive IP stacks. That is to say, you get your own IP stack, now you can ping and be secure because you've got your own IP stack. And we will do anti-spoofing and so on, but this is right now, it's a build time option.
cues.zh: 它实际上给 jails 加上了独占 IP 栈，确实挺令人兴奋。这是其中之一，等会儿讲 zones 时会再回来细说；但这是 zones 明确启发了 jails 的一个领域。最初做这项工作的人说，我们想通过加入独占 IP 栈，让它更像 zones。也就是说，你有了自己的 IP 栈，现在你可以 ping，而且更安全，因为你有自己的 IP 栈。我们还会做防欺骗等等，但目前这还是一个构建时选项。

cues.en: and it's considered experimental, but it seems like it's been around for a while, so I'm not sure what the status is with that. And then you go to the free NAS man page, and they're like, just turn this on, this is fine. It's like, okay, can someone correct someone else's man page, please? So I'm not sure what the deal is with that, but definitely.
cues.zh: 而且它被认为是实验性的，但看起来已经存在一段时间了，所以我不确定它的状态如何。是的，我看到的原始演讲是在 2012 年，看起来已经存在一段时间了，我不确定；但它似乎也不像……IO Cage 的手册页写着，这绝对不能用于生产环境。然后你去看 FreeNAS 的手册页，他们却说，直接打开这个就行，没问题。这就有点……好吧，能不能请人改改别人的手册页？所以我不确定这到底怎么回事，但肯定……

cues.en: These are all really good steps forward for jails, so great to see. And again, I don't want to, by the way, come across as bagging on jails, because jails were very, very, very, very important. It's an extremely good idea, and it was a very directly inspiring idea. So I really do not want to be, I think jails is great, and I think it's been terrific, and I hope that they continue to add all this stuff, because I think it's really important to have.
cues.zh: 这些都是 jails 向前迈出的非常好的步伐，很高兴看到。顺便说一句，我不想显得在贬低 jails，因为 jails 非常、非常、非常、非常重要。这是个极好的想法，而且是一个非常直接的启发来源。所以我真的不想……我觉得 jails 很棒，一直都很出色，我希望他们继续加入所有这些功能，因为我觉得这真的很重要。

cues.en: So that's jails. And jails is very important. And then we get to a couple years later. So I'll tell you what happened inside a sun. And this is where I got a little more...
cues.zh: 这就是 jails。jails 非常重要。然后过了几年。我来告诉你们 Sun 内部发生了什么。这也是我稍微更多……

cues.en: personal experience, so I worked at Sun at the time, worked at Sun, as Ryan mentioned, and started at Sun in 1996, and worked all the way through the dot-com boom and bust, which is actually gonna come up in this paper, believe it or not, if you read the paper very closely. The actual, it's like, it's funny, you know, for those of you who are too young to remember the last bust and don't realize that, like, winter is coming, like, what's winter? It's like, winter is coming, winter is coming, winter is coming.
cues.zh: 亲身经历。当时我在 Sun 工作，正如 Ryan 提到的，我在 Sun 工作，1996 年入职 Sun，一路经历了互联网泡沫的兴衰；信不信由你，如果你仔细读论文，这其实会在论文里出现。其实，这挺有意思的，你们那些太年轻、不记得上次泡沫破灭的人，可能没有意识到，就像“凛冬将至”，冬天是什么？就像，凛冬将至，凛冬将至，凛冬将至。

cues.en: Build a burrow. Build a burrow. Winter is coming. And every once in a while, you get this flurry that blows through. It's like Tableau drops 50% value. Is that a snowflake? It's a beautiful day. What was that? It's like, that's winter, child. That's winter. Winter is coming. So as someone once told me, enjoy the party, but dance close to the door. So as long as you enjoy the party, that's great. Just be ready to run for your life.
cues.zh: 挖个洞穴。挖个洞穴。凛冬将至。每隔一段时间，就会有一阵风雪刮过。就像 Tableau 市值跌了 50%。那是雪花吗？今天天气真好。刚才那是什么？这就是冬天，孩子。这就是冬天。凛冬将至。所以，就像有人曾告诉我的，享受派对，但跳舞时靠近门口。只要你在享受派对，那就很好。只要准备好随时逃命就行。

cues.en: So I worked at Sun during the .com boom and bust, and what we had done, it's kind of interesting, and the reason I came to Sun actually is because Sun in the mid-90s really believed in OS innovation. Every other place that I talked to was just trying to outsource their OS. Oh, to Linux. No, not to Linux. To Windows. It was a dark time. It was a dark, dark, dark time. To Windows. The makers of DOS.
cues.zh: 所以我在 .com 泡沫起伏期在 Sun 工作，我们当时做的事情挺有意思的，而这正是我加入 Sun 的原因——90 年代中期的 Sun 真心相信操作系统创新。我聊过的其他公司都想着把操作系统外包出去。哦，外包给 Linux。不，不是 Linux，是 Windows。那是个黑暗的时代，一个非常、非常、非常黑暗的时代。外包给 Windows，那个 DOS 的缔造者。

cues.en: I said, don't worry, we got this one. It's like, you actually don't. You actually don't. You honestly don't. And I would go interview with all these computer companies, and I mean, it was all, they're very defeatist, and we're like, oh, no, Windows is gonna wear it. It's like, no, no, actually, no. And Sun was the only company, it's like, no, actually, Windows needs to die. We're gonna compete with Windows. We are gonna, Windows needs to die. We're gonna compete with Windows. We believe in the operating system. And when I walked into, you know, Bonwick's office, interviewing at Sun, and at the time I kind of interviewed other groups at Sun, and
cues.zh: 我说，别担心，这个我们搞定了。对方说，你们真搞不定。真的搞不定，说真的，搞不定。我去各家计算机公司面试，大家都特别悲观，都说：唉，Windows 终将赢得一切。我心想：不，不，才不是这样。只有 Sun 这家公司说：不，Windows 必须死。我们要和 Windows 竞争。我们必须——Windows 必须死，我们要和 Windows 竞争。我们相信操作系统。当我走进 Bonwick 在 Sun 的办公室面试时——我之前也面试过 Sun 的其他团队，感觉就像去车管所办业务，毕竟是大公司，不同团队差别很大，有的团队就像：“谁去把 Bob 叫醒，键盘声都响了，好吧。”

cues.en: Kind of felt like interviewing at the DMV because it's a big company and you get different groups and some groups are kind of like, you know, someone wake Bob up, the keyboard's going, you know, all right. But then I walked into Bondworks office and it was like a bolt of lightning and energy and enthusiasm and belief in the ability to innovate in the operating system, emphatic belief. And what I saw is that is what I wanted to go to. I wanted to go innovate in the operating system and there were two companies I found that actually believed in OS innovation in 1996.
cues.zh: 但当我走进 Bonwick 的办公室，就像被闪电击中一样，满是一股干劲、热情，以及对操作系统创新能力的坚定信念。我看到的就是我想要的。我想去搞操作系统创新，而在 1996 年，我只找到两家真正相信操作系统创新的公司。

cues.en: One of them was son. The other one was B. And you're like, B? Yeah, exactly. All right, you need to have the, you know, get the lighter going for B. B, yeah, B, and you're like, B, like a bumblebee? No, no, no, no, like the verb to be, like the verb to be. Well, it was like, it was before Google, okay? No one bothered to like make their names Googleable.
cues.zh: 一家是 Sun，另一家是 Be。你可能会问，Be？对，没错。好了，你得给 Be 点个赞。Be，对。你会想，Be？像大黄蜂那样？不不不，是动词 "to be" 的那个 be。那可是 Google 出现之前的事，好吗？那时候没人费心取一个方便搜索引擎搜到的名字。

cues.en: So, B was a really interesting company. B was developing their own hardware and their own operating system, BIOS, which I thought was very interesting. They were very invested in it. It was a bunch of Apple refugees. And I interviewed at B. It was a start-up, very kind of exciting. And I interviewed with a guy at B. And he was an ex-SGI, super sharp guy. And I actually liked him a lot. And actually, it was kind of an interesting moment. The reason I decided not to go to B is because at the end of the interview, he's like, look, I'm going to level with you.
cues.zh: Be 是一家非常有意思的公司。Be 在开发自己的硬件和自己的操作系统 BeOS，我觉得非常有趣。他们投入很大，核心成员是一群从 Apple 出走的人。我去 Be 面试了，那是一家创业公司，非常令人兴奋。面试我的是一位前 SGI 的家伙，脑子特别快，我其实挺喜欢他的。那是一个挺特别的时刻——我最终决定不去 Be 的原因，是因为面试结束时他说：这样吧，我跟你说实话。

cues.en: I like you a lot. You're a great fit. I need you to come here. I need you to come here. And I'm kind of like, okay, okay, that's cool. Got it. Got it. You need me. That's got it. It's like, I need you to come here because all of these people are from Apple. He's from SGI, right? They're from Apple. Like, I am the only growing up here. I'm like, I'm 22 and you think I look young now. I mean, I look like, I look like an eight year old. I mean, it's
cues.zh: 我很喜欢你。你很合适。我需要你来这儿。我需要你来这儿。我当时有点想，好吧好吧，挺酷的。懂了。懂了。你需要我。这就对了。就像，我需要你来这儿，因为这些人全来自 Apple。他来自 SGI，对吧？他们来自 Apple。我是这儿唯一一个还在长大的人。我才 22 岁，你觉得我现在看起来年轻。我是说，我看起来像，像个八岁小孩。我是说，这……

cues.en: Like a tall eight-year-old. He's like, I need you to come here. So you and I together. Honestly, this is what he said. You and I together can teach them about signal semantics. And I'm like, what screwed up mission is that? I mean, like, I'm going to teach them. Like, talk about, I feel like this is like asking an atheist to go to the Congo and convert people. Like, no! Signal semantics are stupid. I don't want to...
cues.zh: 像个高个儿的八岁小孩。他说，我需要你来这儿。所以你和我一起。说实话，他原话就是这样。你和我一起能教他们信号语义。我就想，这什么鬼任务？我是说，就像，我要去教他们。就像，怎么说呢，我感觉这就像让一个无神论者去刚果传教。就像，不！信号语义蠢透了。我不想……

cues.en: I mean, if you know anything about unique signal semantics, you probably can't talk about it because you begin to blackout. I mean, signal semantics, there's so much that's broken with them. I certainly don't want to be preaching a good book of signal semantics to a bunch of apple refugees. I mean, I honestly sound like a suicide pact. So I'm like, okay, that's cool, that's cool, that's cool.
cues.zh: 我是说，如果你了解一点独特的信号语义，你大概都没法谈它，因为你会开始断片。我是说，信号语义，坏掉的地方太多了。我当然不想向一群 Apple 难民宣讲信号语义的福音。我是说，这听起来真像自杀协议。所以我就想，好吧，挺酷的，挺酷的，挺酷的。

cues.en: By the way, never say that to a 22-year-old. I got it. You got a crush on me, but let's dial it down a little bit. Let's not name the babies yet. Especially, let's not name the babies that. Wait, we're naming our oldest Sig action? Are you kidding me? Oh, little Sig action. It's like, okay, this place is too warped. I'm out of here. Sig IO, come on. Come on, Sig IO. Where's Sig IO? We've lost Sig IO. Of course, you've lost Sig IO.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，永远别对 22 岁的人说那种话。我懂了。你迷上我了，但咱们收敛一点。先别急着给孩子起名。尤其是，别给孩子起那种名字。等等，我们给老大起名叫 Sig action？开什么玩笑？哦，小 Sig action。就像，好吧，这地方太扭曲了。我走了。Sig IO，拜托。拜托，Sig IO。Sig IO 在哪儿？我们把 Sig IO 弄丢了。当然了，你们把 Sig IO 弄丢了。

cues.en: Stupid! So, okay, SigAction can't do anything, right? You know, it's like, you could make a whole sitcom about, you know, the signals. Anyway, so you win. Signal exists, but it's kind of like the fossil is dead anyway, whatever. So I did not work for B, and actually kind of a funny, the funny kind of epilogue on B. So I didn't work for B. B goes out of business. I, in the dot-com bust, I go to the B bankruptcy auction, which is...
cues.zh: 蠢死了！所以，好吧，SigAction 什么都干不了，对吧？你知道，就像，你完全可以围绕这些信号拍一整部情景喜剧。总之，你赢了。信号是存在的，但反正像化石一样死了，随便吧。所以我没为 B 工作，而且这事后来还有个挺好笑的尾声。所以我没为 B 工作。B 倒闭了。在互联网泡沫破灭时，我去了 B 的破产拍卖会，那真是……

cues.en: is a really, it's a fascinating thing to actually do. I mean, it's a little bit like you feel like you are devouring this, or watching a corpse be devoured on the Serengeti. Because when these companies finally fall over and die...
cues.zh: 真的是，亲身经历还挺奇妙的。我是说，有点像你觉得自己在吞噬它，或者在塞伦盖蒂看一具尸体被吞噬。因为当这些公司终于倒下死掉时……

cues.en: They get descended upon by these office furniture consolidators. And this is relatively early in the bus. This is going to be like maybe 2000, 2001. I can't remember when exactly it was. And so I'm at the B bankruptcy auction. I just kind of wanted to check it out. I also, I secretly was hoping I could get some manuals. I like computer manuals. I'm kind of that guy. And they had some
cues.zh: 它们会被这些办公家具整合商一拥而上地瓜分。这在泡沫破灭里算比较早期。大概可能是 2000、2001 年吧。我记不清具体是哪年了。所以我在 B 的破产拍卖会上。我就是有点想去看看。我还偷偷希望能弄到一些手册。我喜欢电脑手册。我差不多就是那种人。而且他们有些

cues.en: weird, weird, weird CPUs. So if you remember, they ran before. They kind of ran on more mainstream stuff. They ran on the Exponential X704 PowerPC clone. And then they ran on the AT&T Hobbit.
cues.zh: 怪怪怪的 CPU。所以如果你还记得，他们以前跑过。他们大概跑在更主流的东西上。他们跑过 Exponential X704 PowerPC 克隆。后来又跑在 AT&T Hobbit 上。

cues.en: which is the weirdest microprocessor you've never heard of. Yeah, exactly. Stack-based architecture, really, really weird. I kind of accrue up a log on that microprocessor, which is a terribly misdesigned microprocessor. The lead architect for that then came to work at Sun on Cheetah, the most cruelly named microprocessor in human history. It's like, is this like dead cheetah, rotting cheetah? Is this paraplegic cheetah? I mean, paraplegic cheetah, I can get that, maybe. Anyway, Cheetah was not a cheetah. So I'm going to this, and I find...
cues.zh: 这是你没听说过的最古怪的微处理器。对，没错。基于栈的架构，真的真的很怪。我算是写了一篇关于那款微处理器的博客，它设计得极其糟糕。那款芯片的首席架构师后来去了 Sun，参与 Cheetah——人类历史上命名最残忍的微处理器。就像，这是死猎豹、腐烂的猎豹吗？这是瘫痪的猎豹吗？我是说，瘫痪的猎豹，也许我还能理解。总之，Cheetah 并不是猎豹。所以我去到这个……然后我发现……

cues.en: this box that has all of these manuals in it. I'm just like, oh, this is great. But the box has got no label on it. And I'm like, I will bid $10,000 in this box.
cues.zh: 这个箱子，里面全是这些手册。我就想，哦，太棒了。但箱子上面没有标签。然后我就想，我要为这个箱子出价 1 万美元。

cues.en: Like I am a loaded for bear. I'm kind of like talking myself into it. I'm like, no that's stupid. No, this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. This is a Hobbit manual. This is worth a King's ransom. It's like, it's worth a King's ransom to you, you idiot. It's not worth a penny to anybody else, which I found out like 10 seconds later when I finally found the auctioneer like, like, how do I bid on this? And he's like, he's kind of looking at the number. He's like, just take it. And I'm like, is this stealing?
cues.zh: 我简直是有备而来。我有点在说服自己。我想，不，那太蠢了。不，这是千载难逢的机会。这是 Hobbit 手册。这值一笔国王级赎金。就像，它对你值一笔国王级赎金，你这个白痴。对别人来说它一文不值。大约 10 秒后我就发现了，当时我终于找到拍卖师，问，呃，这个怎么出价？他就像，他看着号码。他说，直接拿走。我就想，这算偷吗？

cues.en: I will just take it. I'm like, oh my, oh my God. I like hit jackpot at the B bankruptcy auction. It's like, wow, you are in a small demographic. But we, I also, I also ended up buying like eight whiteboards for a buck. It had so many whiteboards there. And so we, I get that we get this whiteboard up to our apartment and by the way, like much of D-Trace, well, actually this is true. D-Trace was, was, was designed and implemented on a dead B whiteboard. A little trivia for you.
cues.zh: 那我就直接拿走。我就想，天啊，我的天。我简直是在 B 的破产拍卖上中了头奖。就像，哇，你属于很小的一群人。但我们，我也，我最后还花一美元买了大约八块白板。那里有好多白板。于是我们，我把这块白板弄回公寓，顺便说一句，D-Trace 的很多部分，嗯，其实这是真的。D-Trace 是在一块废弃的 B 白板上设计和实现的。给你们讲个小趣闻。

cues.en: All right, so in our apartment we used these whiteboards, we had big ones, we had small ones, it was great. And one of the whiteboards still needed to be erased. Like, okay, we'll erase this. You go to erase it and you're like, oh, it's that whiteboard. It's the permanent microwave. Someone at B, at some point in time, wrote up about two-thirds of the B VFS architecture in a permanent marker before realizing, oh, God, damn it! I mean, you can just envision it. You can just envision it.
cues.zh: 好，在我们公寓里我们用这些白板，大的小的都有，很棒。其中一块白板还需要擦掉。就像，好，我们把这擦了。你去擦的时候就会想，哦，就是那块白板。这是那支永久记号笔。B 的某个人在某个时候用永久记号笔写了大约三分之二的 B VFS 架构，然后才意识到，哦，天哪，该死！我是说，你完全能想象出来。你完全能想象出来。

cues.en: And so I'm like, not only did I get a whiteboard, I got like a free VFS architecture, like two thirds of it anyway. And so when we was finally trying to leave that apartment and we were giving away all these whiteboards, I'm like, this whiteboard is a special whiteboard. cues.zh: 他们修复了这个问题，我觉得很好。我认为这是正确答案。顺便说一句，多年以后，我认为那绝对是正确的决定。所以就 IPC 而言，IPC 机制会按你预期的方式工作。非常重要的是，System 5 IPC 会按你预期的方式工作。所以 System 5 IPC 在 pay rate 里被特意点名。它值得用一段话说明。它确实很重要。在网络方面，我们看到了和 jails 相同的一些问题。我们有一个共享的网络栈。

cues.zh: 那个共享网络栈不允许我们使用原始套接字。我们不给原始套接字访问权限，但他们明确允许 ICMP。所以他们额外做了工作来允许 ICMP，这有点像，我的意思是，这又是另一个例子：其实不是全有或全无。你实际上可以做些工程工作，安全地允许 ICMP，安全地允许 traceroute，安全地允许 ping，但不允许其他东西。

cues.zh: 那个 zone 就能伪造它的流量，随意冒用任意 IP 地址。当然，系统对此是有警告的。所幸他们确实加入了防欺骗功能。防欺骗对于安全部署至关重要。这是通过 Crossbow 实现的，非常棒。我们在资源管理方面做了大量工作，包括更完善的内存上限、CPU 上限、I/O 限流等等。然后当然还有 CFS。这篇论文完全没有提及 CFS，因为当时 CFS 还没公开。这就是为什么论文没提 CFS，在提交论文时它既未集成也未公开。
